resources.string: Point CHDBOY at a folder and it converts every ISO, CUE and GDI image inside it to CHD. Each CHD is written alongside the image it came from, and the originals are left untouched.
Compresses on every CPU core at once with zstd, so it runs as fast as your device allows.
Reads each disc to work out whether it needs CD or DVD handling, so you never have to pick.
Leaves images that already have a CHD alone, so running it twice on the same folder costs nothing.
Removes a disc image and its track files once its CHD has been written. Skipped if the conversion fails.

A disc image can take several minutes to compress, and CHDBOY keeps going while you use other apps.

• Live progress while a folder converts
• A summary when the run finishes

resources.string:
CHDBOY losslessly compresses BIN/CUE, GDI and ISO disc images into CHD archives.

Highlights:

• Compresses on every core at once, using zstd
• Reads and writes in place, so no temporary copies
• Stores repeated data once across the whole image
• Writes proper CD track metadata for CUE and GDI
• Skips files that already have matching CHDs

Originally forked from Pipetto-crypto/Chdman. The CHD format is from the MAME project; decoding and CD-ROM ECC come from libchdr, and compression from zstd.
